bull.t: Strong gross margin and permanent cost reductions
bull.b: The nearly 50% gross margin provides a solid base for eventual profitability, while permanent workforce and operating-cost reductions can lower the break-even point if residential solar volumes recover.

bull.t: Fresh capital supports near-term operating flexibility
bull.b: The combined $5.5M of new financing modestly strengthens liquidity and provides additional time to execute its turnaround. Insider participation also indicates management is willing to commit capital during the restructuring.

bull.t: Established residential solar platform and customer channels
bull.b: A multi-channel residential platform, supported by direct sales and dealer relationships, can broaden customer access and create recurring service opportunities as household solar and storage adoption expands.

bear.t: Persistent losses and substantial cash burn
bear.b: The core business is still consuming significant cash while operating losses persist. Without a sustained return to positive cash generation, SunPower may remain dependent on external financing to fund operations.

bear.t: Negative equity and elevated balance-sheet risk
bear.b: The equity deficit weakens financial resilience and limits flexibility when operations deteriorate. Meaningful debt relative to the capital base increases sensitivity to refinancing needs, losses, and further funding requirements.

bear.t: Nasdaq listing compliance and execution pressures
bear.b: The listing deficiency creates a regulatory milestone that may require costly capital-structure action if unresolved. Delayed jobs and quality-control lapses also indicate execution weaknesses that can hinder revenue conversion.
